headline: One Bet, One Win, And A Perfect Week Worth Nine Dollars
paragraphs: Two games got graded. One was passed on. That left a single ticket, ten dollars, Under 46 in Kent State at Eastern Michigan, and the model gave itself 56.3 percent on a five point edge. Final was 17 to 12, which clears the number by a distance you could measure with a tape. Profit of $9.09, ROI of 90.9 percent, and a flawless 1-0 record for the week.

That is the entire story, and it is worth being honest about the size of it. A perfect week in the totals market, one play deep, is the betting equivalent of going undefeated in a one game season. The lone line that moved did not move toward the model, which is zero percent of the drift going our way, so the market and the model shook hands and quietly disagreed on the way out the door.

The season ledger does not care about tidy weeks. Ten weeks graded for real, 559 plays, a record of 240-304-15, and a loss of $711.01 at negative 12.7 percent ROI. The model thought it would hit 60.5 percent and hit 44.1. There is also a hindsight graded week sitting off to the side at 40-25-1 and plus $110.47, which is what happens when you fill out a card after the scores are in. It counts for nothing and I am not pretending otherwise.
